Unguarded AIPW estimator

estimate_beta_aipw.Rd

Augmented IPW estimator of \(\theta = (\beta, \sigma)\) with the unguarded augmentation function \(\Psi^{eff}_{AIPW}(Y, Z; \theta)\) of the manuscript, computed by numerical integration over a working model for \(f_{X|Y,Z}\):

fx_method = "joint"

(default; the choice used in the manuscript's simulations and application) Bayes' theorem, \(f_{X|Y,Z} \propto f_{Y|X,Z}(y | x, z; \theta) f_{X|Z}(x; \hat\gamma)\), with \(\hat\gamma\) from the MLE (estimate_beta_mle) unless gamma is supplied.

fx_method = "direct"

\(f_{X|Y,Z}\) is a Weibull AFT model, survreg(Surv(W, D) ~ y + Z), fitted to all rows. Standard survival software can fit this model because \(C\) is independent of \(X\) given \((Y, Z)\); the Weibull form is a working assumption, and the model is misspecified for data from data_aft.

The unguarded AIPW estimator is consistent when the model for \(C | (Y, Z)\) and the mean of the outcome model are correctly specified, whatever the working model for \(f_{X|Y,Z}\). The asymptotic variance of the unguarded AIPW estimator is smaller than that of the IPW estimator when \(f_{X|Y,Z}\) is correctly specified (with fx_method = "joint", when \(f_{Y|X,Z}\) and \(f_{X|Z}\) are) and the parameters of the model for \(C | (Y, Z)\) are independent of \(\theta\); otherwise there is no such guarantee (see estimate_beta_aipw_lambda). The sandwich standard errors account for estimating the weights.

Usage

estimate_beta_aipw(
  data_yXZ,
  model,
  model_xz = NULL,
  model_weights = NULL,
  fx_method = c("joint", "direct"),
  gamma = NULL,
  tau = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  aw_var = "AW",
  a_var = "A"
)

Arguments

data_yXZ

A data frame with one row per subject. It must contain the outcome, the covariates in model, the age a_var, the observed W = min(X, C), and the indicator D = I(X <= C).

model

A formula for the outcome model, y ~ AW + Z1 + ..., with the time-to-event covariate aw_var on the right-hand side. The outcome model is \(Y = \beta_0 + \beta_{A-X} (A - X) + \beta_Z' Z + \epsilon\), \(\epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\).

model_xz

A one-sided formula for the Weibull AFT model of \(X | Z\), for example ~ Z. Defaults to the covariates of model other than aw_var.

model_weights

A one-sided formula for the Weibull AFT model of \(C | (Y, Z)\), for example ~ y + Z. Defaults to the outcome and the covariates of model other than aw_var.

fx_method

"joint" or "direct"; see Details.

gamma

Optional coefficients and scale of the Weibull model for \(X | Z\) (as in estimate_beta_mle()$gamma_est). Used only with fx_method = "joint"; if NULL, the MLE is fitted first.

tau

Optional upper limit of the integral over \(X\). The estimator stays consistent for any tau; a finite tau only changes the working model. Useful when the integral is unstable in the right tail.

start

Optional starting value for \((\beta, \sigma)\). Defaults to the IPW estimate.

aw_var

Name of the column A - W in model. Defaults to "AW".

a_var

Name of the age column A. Defaults to "A".

Value

A list with beta_est, se_est, converged, and fx_par (the parameters of the working model for \(f_{X|Y,Z}\)).

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
dat <- data_aft(500)
estimate_beta_aipw(dat, y ~ AW + Z, model_xz = ~ Z, model_weights = ~ y + Z)
#> $beta_est
#> (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma 
#>   0.9859697   1.0000872   1.0347681   1.0072679 
#> 
#> $se_est
#> (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma 
#>  0.07536479  0.04727333  0.04879631  0.03559105 
#> 
#> $converged
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $fx_par
#> (Intercept)           Z       scale 
#>  0.09482263  0.11804817  0.46886206 
#> 
estimate_beta_aipw(dat, y ~ AW + Z, fx_method = "direct")
#> $beta_est
#> (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma 
#>   1.0030499   0.9950320   1.0395196   0.9907767 
#> 
#> $se_est
#> (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma 
#>  0.07124585  0.04543260  0.04965520  0.03788816 
#> 
#> $converged
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $fx_par
#> (Intercept)           y           Z       scale 
#>   0.3440334  -0.1310271   0.2229283   0.4463420 
#> 
# }
